I've been farming this land in Quzhou County for over fifty years, and I know what works here on the North China Plain. The soil is good, but the seasons are tight — you have to plant winter wheat right after the autumn harvest and then rush to get summer maize in the ground as soon as the wheat comes off in June. At my age, I don't have the energy to experiment with new crops or fancy techniques. I stick to what I know: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That's the backbone of every farm around here.

I'll plant my winter wheat on 4 mu. I'll use the same improved Jinmai variety I've been using for years — the seed dealer says it's good, and it always gives me a decent harvest if the winter isn't too cruel. For fertilizer, I'll put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. I know the land needs feeding if it's going to feed me. I'll irrigate three times — once after planting to get the seedlings up, once at the overwintering stage if it's too dry, and once at the jointing stage in spring when the wheat really starts to shoot up. I'll spray pesticides twice, mainly to keep away the aphids and rust that always seem to find my fields. I'll do rotary tillage before planting the wheat to break up the corn stubble from last season.

For summer maize, I'll also plant 4 mu right after the wheat harvest. I'll use hybrid seed — everybody uses hybrid corn now because the yield is so much better than the old traditional types. I'll give it 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. The maize needs two good irrigations, one right after planting and another at the big trumpet stage when the ears are forming. I'll spray pesticides twice for the corn borers and armyworms that come every summer. I'll do rotary tillage again before drilling the maize.

I expect my wheat to yield around 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates, and the maize should give me about 550 kg per mu. Between the two crops, I'll have enough grain to sell some and keep some for my family. This is the same plan I've made for decades, and it has kept me going.
